summary: An outstanding, well-researched ethics report. You thoroughly identified the ethical issues, organisational context and stakeholders, and built balanced, evidence-based arguments with quantitative support. Your decision rule, option table and multi-stakeholder recommendations flow logically to a justified conclusion. Only minor formatting and abstract-length issues prevented a perfect structure mark.
next_steps: Trim the abstract to the ~150-word target; it currently runs to about 170 words.
Standardise heading levels throughout (you mix ####/#####/### inconsistently) and check they follow your template's hierarchy.
Add one or two more visual element types (e.g., a stakeholder influence map or timeline) to complement Figure 1 and Tables 1–2.

criteria.C1: Excellent work. You identified several ethical issues (test coverage driven by schedule, data-loss/harm, conflict of interest), framed them as organisational design-process decisions, and your Table 1 clearly mapped stakeholders, their stakes and decision control. To sustain this level, keep explicitly linking each new issue back to both organisational context and stakeholder interests as you did here.
criteria.C2: Excellent. Your arguments for and against shipping were objective, evidence-based and appropriately deep, and your recommendations addressed Rachel, management, the health department, the chip supplier and engineers. Maintain this breadth by always asking which stakeholders a conclusion serves, as your RECOMMENDATIONS section successfully did.
criteria.C3: Excellent. The body's structure — for-arguments, systematic rebuttals, the Figure 1 decision rule, and the Table 2 trade-off analysis — built compellingly to your conclusion that Options B and C best respect all stakeholders. Keep using this pattern of argument-then-rebuttal to make future conclusions equally well supported.
criteria.C4: Excellent research. Eight reputable references (NAO, Leveson & Turner, Intel, DOJ, Standards Australia, EA Code, HBR) combined quantitative evidence (81/236 trusts, 19,000 cancelled appointments, US$475M, US$4.3B) with qualitative case analysis, and you appropriately caveated the WannaCry cause distinction. Continue balancing both evidence types in future work.
criteria.C5: Very good. Your writing is fluent and concise, IEEE references are consistently formatted, and Figure 1 and Tables 1–2 are used competently. To reach the excellent level: fix the inconsistent heading levels, tighten the abstract to ~150 words, and incorporate a wider variety of visual elements.
